To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Overall assessment:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" from the Buyer's side. It collapses every protection into a single 20%/18-month general regime, pushes two closing-critical items (Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge) past Completion, and leaves at least AUD 930,000 of identified leakage (bonuses, Ironquay, Sandbar) unaddressed in a debt-free/cash-free deal. Several items below should be treated as conditions or price adjustments, not warranty matters.

---

## Liability regime

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- *Buyer wants:* General cap of 30–50% (AUD 7.2m–12m), with fundamental warranties, Tax warranties and specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) outside or at 100% of price.
- *Recommendation:* Counter at 40% (AUD 9.6m), with tax/IP and specific indemnities carved out of the general cap. — Reason: 20% is below market for a ~AUD 24m private M&A deal with known, unresolved risks concentrated in a single 30% customer and unverified IP.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25,000 (~0.1%); basket AUD 250,000 (~1.04%), excess-only (deductible).
- *Buyer wants:* De minimis AUD 10,000–12,000; basket AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%); tipping (first-dollar) basket; related claims aggregated; de minimis and basket not to apply to fundamental, tax or specific-indemnity claims.
- *Recommendation:* Accept de minimis at AUD 15,000 with aggregation of a series of related claims; move basket to tipping at AUD 240,000 (1%). — Reason: a deductible basket at 1% plus a high de minimis effectively gives the Seller a second cap on the smaller, more probable claims.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months from Completion; limitation to apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- *Buyer wants:* 24 months for general warranties (allows one full audit cycle plus a buffer); tax 7 years (or statutory period + 6 months); fundamental/title 6–7 years; specific indemnities with no limit or 6 years; delete the "applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise" default.
- *Recommendation:* Counter at 24 months general / 7 years tax and fundamental, and reverse the default so limits apply only where expressly stated. — Reason: 18 months expires before the first full post-completion audit of FY27 accounts is complete, and the "all Claims" default would silently sweep in indemnity and fundamental claims.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity".
- *Buyer wants:* Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) capped at 100% of price, surviving 6–7 years, not subject to de minimis/basket or disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* Reject outright; this is non-negotiable. — Reason: if the Buyer does not get good title to 100% of the shares, recovering only 20% of the price after 18 months is not a remedy — it's a 80% loss.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). No fraud carve-out appears anywhere in the package.
- *Buyer wants:* Express carve-out from all caps, thresholds, time limits, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clauses for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or (with knowledge) the Company's key personnel.
- *Recommendation:* Insist on a full fraud/wilful misconduct carve-out; non-negotiable. — Reason: a limitation clause purporting to cap or exclude fraud is unlikely to be enforceable in NSW anyway, so the Seller loses nothing legitimate by conceding it, and its absence is a red flag.

---

## Disclosure & knowledge

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and all "publicly searchable corporate records" (DL 1.1–1.2); plus a reservation that nothing is admitted (DL 1.4).
- *Buyer wants:* Disclosure limited to matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed"; no general disclosure of public registers (or, at most, ASIC company extract and PPSR search as at a fixed date); data room disclosure only via an indexed, agreed USB/schedule with the index attached to the Disclosure Letter; no disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax warranties or specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* Reject general disclosure of public records entirely; accept data-room disclosure only with a "fair disclosure" standard and an agreed index. — Reason: blanket disclosure of a 12-item data room plus every public register would gut the warranties, since any matter the Buyer *could* have found becomes disclosed whether or not it was fairly identified.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- *Buyer wants:* Delete cl 8.3, or confine it to actual knowledge of a named list of 2–3 deal team members, excluding advisers and excluding constructive/"discoverable" knowledge; expressly confirm that the Buyer's DD and the matters in DD-002 to DD-012 do not prejudice claims.
- *Recommendation:* Delete; fall back only to actual knowledge of named individuals with no adviser imputation and no "discoverable" limb. — Reason: "discoverable" is constructive knowledge and combined with SPA-N-006 would mean the Buyer can never claim on anything in the data room — which is where every identified problem sits.

---

## Closing-critical / price items

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* "Reasonable endeavours"; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions have been met.
- *Buyer wants:* Bluefen consent as a true condition precedent to Completion (not waivable by the Seller), satisfied only by unconditional written consent *and* evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived by Bluefen; Seller to use "best endeavours"; Buyer walk right / long-stop date; if consent is conditional on commercial concessions, those are for the Seller's account or a price adjustment.
- *Recommendation:* Hard CP with unconditional consent and satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions, plus a termination right. — Reason: Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; losing it on a change-of-control trigger would impair roughly a third of the value being paid for.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). Disclosure Letter confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room, and change-of-control (cl 8.1) exists.
- *Buyer wants:* Full repayment and executed discharge/release of all security (including PPSR releases and any guarantees) delivered *at* Completion as a Completion deliverable, with the payout figure deducted from the price via the debt-free/cash-free mechanism and paid directly to Riverlark from the funds flow; Riverlark consent or waiver of cl 8.1 obtained pre-Completion.
- *Recommendation:* Reject post-Completion release; require payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge at Completion, funded from the purchase price. — Reason: the deal is debt-free/cash-free, so a AUD 3.2m facility still secured over the Company after Completion — and potentially in default under cl 8.1 on the share sale — is a direct AUD 3.2m hole in the Buyer's price.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter confirms they are not in the funds flow and is silent on superannuation, payroll tax and on-costs.
- *Buyer wants:* Bonuses (plus super at 12%, payroll tax at ~5.45% NSW, and any other on-costs — realistically AUD ~490,000–500,000 all-in) treated as Transaction Costs/Debt in the Completion Accounts and deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller through the funds flow at Completion; indemnity for any shortfall; confirmation of who bears the employer obligations if the "continued employment" condition is triggered post-Completion.
- *Recommendation:* Itemise in the funds flow as a price deduction grossed up for super and payroll tax, with a specific indemnity. — Reason: a Completion bonus payable by the Company is a liability that crystallises on the Buyer's watch, and "a matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the funds actually leave the Seller's side of the ledger.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment (cl 11.1) and "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 open per DD-010; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Pre-Completion settlement of the AUD 180,000 and delivery of a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable; failing that, a specific indemnity covering (a) all SOW3 fees and any further sums Ironquay demands, (b) loss arising from any defect in title to or infringement claims over the Project Materials, and (c) costs of re-procuring or re-developing the materials — uncapped or capped at 100% of price, not subject to basket/de minimis, surviving 6 years.
- *Recommendation:* Make payment and confirmatory assignment a Completion deliverable, and widen the indemnity to cover title to the Project Materials, not just the payment. — Reason: the risk is not the AUD 180,000 — it is that the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables at all until payment clears, and an indemnity for a known cheque doesn't cover loss of the IP.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- *Seller:* DD-006 is a "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). Disclosure Letter: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed, scope or notification required; investigation preliminary.
- *Buyer wants:* Completion of the investigation before Completion with a written report; a specific indemnity for all costs, OAIC/regulatory penalties, Notifiable Data Breach scheme notification costs, third-party claims and remediation arising from the incident (and any other pre-Completion breach), outside the cap/basket/time limits; a warranty that no other incidents exist; ability for the Buyer to control any notification post-Completion with Seller funding it.
- *Recommendation:* Specific, uncapped (or 100%-capped) indemnity plus a pre-Completion investigation report deliverable. — Reason: an unresolved potential eligible data breach of ~1,240 individuals' data carries regulatory and reputational exposure that cannot be measured yet, which is precisely why it must sit outside a 20%/18-month general regime.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure Letter concedes it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course, and that DD-008/DD-011 must be read together.
- *Buyer wants:* Clarification of timing (pre- or post-Completion), whether the three contracts are related/linked and why they're split into three at an identical figure; any amounts committed or accrued pre-Completion but unpaid to be treated as Debt or Working Capital in the Completion Accounts; Seller warranty that no other related renewals exist; Buyer consent to any renewal between signing and Completion under the gap covenants.
- *Recommendation:* Require full disclosure of the Sandbar contracts and treat any pre-Completion commitment as a Completion Accounts adjustment; add renewals to the interim-period consent list. — Reason: three identical AUD 110k commitments split across two data-room documents looks like structuring below a materiality threshold, and "ordinary course" is an assertion the Seller's own Disclosure Letter declines to support.

---

## Structural items

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* One regime: all Claims of any nature subject to the same cap, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3/12.3/12.8/13/20.5); title and capacity folded in; tax and IP "settled under the general regime".
- *Buyer wants:* Four distinct claim categories, each with its own cap, time limit and threshold treatment:
  1. General warranties — 40% cap, 24 months, basket/de minimis apply.
  2. Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share capital) — 100% cap, 6–7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure.
  3. Tax warranties and tax indemnity — 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure.
  4. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, any Bluefen concessions) — 100% cap or uncapped, 6 years, no thresholds, no disclosure, no knowledge qualifier.
  Plus a global fraud carve-out and an overall aggregate cap at 100% of price.
- *Recommendation:* Restructure cl 12/13 into separate categories; reject "all Claims unless expressly stated". — Reason: the Seller's "administrative simplicity" is a single 20% cap on everything, which is the mechanism by which every other issue in this memo gets neutralised.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title to 100% of shares "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012". Disclosure Letter states this is the source relied on and does not state the Buyer has verified it.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract and historical extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (noting Riverlark's security), review of share certificates, constitution (pre-emption/transfer restrictions), any shareholder agreements, and chain of title since incorporation; unqualified fundamental warranties on title, no encumbrances and no options/convertibles; Completion deliverables to include executed transfers, share certificates, register updates and ASIC Form 484 lodgement.
- *Recommendation:* Run ASIC/PPSR searches now, confirm no share security to Riverlark, and keep title warranties absolute and outside the cap. — Reason: a company's own share register is maintained by the Seller's directors and is not independent evidence; with AUD 3.2m of secured debt outstanding, a charge over the shares themselves is a live possibility.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* "Settled under the general regime" — i.e., 20% cap, 18 months, basket/de minimis, general disclosure and the knowledge qualifier all apply.
- *Buyer wants:* **Tax:** a standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, including under the Completion Accounts cut-off) and full tax warranties, 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure; pre-Completion tax returns and ATO correspondence reviewed. **IP:** full IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, all contractor/employee IP assigned, open-source compliance, Ironquay chain of title), with a separate cap (100%) and 6-year period given the business is an analytics company whose value is its IP and data.
- *Recommendation:* Treat tax and IP as open, not settled; carve both out of the general regime with their own caps and periods. — Reason: the Seller's own Disclosure Letter shows IP title to SOW3 is unresolved and is silent on tax entirely, so "settled" simply means "not negotiated".

---

## Priority order for the mark-up

| Priority | Issue | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **Must have (deal-breakers)** | N-004, N-005, N-009, N-008 | Separate fundamental regime; fraud carve-out; Riverlark discharge at Completion; Bluefen as hard CP |
| **Price/funds-flow fixes** | N-010, N-011, N-013 | ~AUD 930k+ of identified leakage to be deducted or indemnified |
| **Regime structure** | N-014, N-001, N-003, N-002, N-016 | Four-category structure; 40% / 24 months / tipping basket |
| **Disclosure hygiene** | N-006, N-007, N-012, N-015 | Fair-disclosure standard; delete cl 8.3; DD-006 indemnity; independent title searches |

**Immediate next steps:** (1) order ASIC and PPSR searches against Paperbark and Harbourglass today; (2) request the Bluefen cl 11.3 condition correspondence and the Riverlark payout figure; (3) ask the Seller for the Sandbar contracts in full and a status update on the DD-006 investigation; (4) build a Completion Accounts/funds-flow schedule showing the Riverlark payoff, grossed-up bonuses and Ironquay payment as deductions.

One caveat: I'm working only from the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA draft or the DD documents themselves. Several recommendations (particularly the Sandbar and Riverlark security points) should be confirmed against the underlying documents before the mark-up goes out.

- *Buyer wants:* Full repayment and executed discharge/release of all security (including PPSR releases and any guarantees) delivered *at* Completion as a Completion deliverable, with the payout figure deducted from the price via the debt-free/cash-free mechanism and paid directly to Riverlark from the funds flow; Riverlark consent or waiver of cl 8.1 obtained pre-Completion.
- *Recommendation:* Reject post-Completion release; require payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge at Completion, funded from the purchase price. — Reason: the deal is debt-free/cash-free, so a AUD 3.2m facility still secured over the Company after Completion — and potentially in default under cl 8.1 on the share sale — is a direct AUD 3.2m hole in the Buyer's price.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter confirms they are not in the funds flow and is silent on superannuation, payroll tax and on-costs.
- *Buyer wants:* Bonuses (plus super at 12%, payroll tax at ~5.45% NSW, and any other on-costs — realistically AUD ~490,000–500,000 all-in) treated as Transaction Costs/Debt in the Completion Accounts and deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller through the funds flow at Completion; indemnity for any shortfall; confirmation of who bears the employer obligations if the "continued employment" condition is triggered post-Completion.
- *Recommendation:* Itemise in the funds flow as a price deduction grossed up for super and payroll tax, with a specific indemnity. — Reason: a Completion bonus payable by the Company is a liability that crystallises on the Buyer's watch, and "a matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the funds actually leave the Seller's side of the ledger.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment (cl 11.1) and "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 open per DD-010; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Pre-Completion settlement of the AUD 180,000 and delivery of a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable; failing that, a specific indemnity covering (a) all SOW3 fees and any further sums Ironquay demands, (b) loss arising from any defect in title to or infringement claims over the Project Materials, and (c) costs of re-procuring or re-developing the materials — uncapped or capped at 100% of price, not subject to basket/de minimis, surviving 6 years.
- *Recommendation:* Make payment and confirmatory assignment a Completion deliverable, and widen the indemnity to cover title to the Project Materials, not just the payment. — Reason: the risk is not the AUD 180,000 — it is that the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables at all until payment clears, and an indemnity for a known cheque doesn't cover loss of the IP.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- *Seller:* DD-006 is a "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). Disclosure Letter: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed, scope or notification required; investigation preliminary.
- *Buyer wants:* Completion of the investigation before Completion with a written report; a specific indemnity for all costs, OAIC/regulatory penalties, Notifiable Data Breach scheme notification costs, third-party claims and remediation arising from the incident (and any other pre-Completion breach), outside the cap/basket/time limits; a warranty that no other incidents exist; ability for the Buyer to control any notification post-Completion with Seller funding it.
- *Recommendation:* Specific, uncapped (or 100%-capped) indemnity plus a pre-Completion investigation report deliverable. — Reason: an unresolved potential eligible data breach of ~1,240 individuals' data carries regulatory and reputational exposure that cannot be measured yet, which is precisely why it must sit outside a 20%/18-month general regime.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure Letter concedes it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course, and that DD-008/DD-011 must be read together.
- *Buyer wants:* Clarification of timing (pre- or post-Completion), whether the three contracts are related/linked and why they're split into three at an identical figure; any amounts committed or accrued pre-Completion but unpaid to be treated as Debt or Working Capital in the Completion Accounts; Seller warranty that no other related renewals exist; Buyer consent to any renewal between signing and Completion under the gap covenants.
- *Recommendation:* Require full disclosure of the Sandbar contracts and treat any pre-Completion commitment as a Completion Accounts adjustment; add renewals to the interim-period consent list. — Reason: three identical AUD 110k commitments split across two data-room documents looks like structuring below a materiality threshold, and "ordinary course" is an assertion the Seller's own Disclosure Letter declines to support.

## Structural items

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* One regime: all Claims of any nature subject to the same cap, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3/12.3/12.8/13/20.5); title and capacity folded in; tax and IP "settled under the general regime".
- *Buyer wants:* Four distinct claim categories, each with its own cap, time limit and threshold treatment:
  1. General warranties — 40% cap, 24 months, basket/de minimis apply.
  2. Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share capital) — 100% cap, 6–7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure.
  3. Tax warranties and tax indemnity — 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure.
  4. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, any Bluefen concessions) — 100% cap or uncapped, 6 years, no thresholds, no disclosure, no knowledge qualifier.
  Plus a global fraud carve-out and an overall aggregate cap at 100% of price.
- *Recommendation:* Restructure cl 12/13 into separate categories; reject "all Claims unless expressly stated". — Reason: the Seller's "administrative simplicity" is a single 20% cap on everything, which is the mechanism by which every other issue in this memo gets neutralised.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title to 100% of shares "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012". Disclosure Letter states this is the source relied on and does not state the Buyer has verified it.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract and historical extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (noting Riverlark's security), review of share certificates, constitution (pre-emption/transfer restrictions), any shareholder agreements, and chain of title since incorporation; unqualified fundamental warranties on title, no encumbrances and no options/convertibles; Completion deliverables to include executed transfers, share certificates, register updates and ASIC Form 484 lodgement.
- *Recommendation:* Run ASIC/PPSR searches now, confirm no share security to Riverlark, and keep title warranties absolute and outside the cap. — Reason: a company's own share register is maintained by the Seller's directors and is not independent evidence; with AUD 3.2m of secured debt outstanding, a charge over the shares themselves is a live possibility.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* "Settled under the general regime" — i.e., 20% cap, 18 months, basket/de minimis, general disclosure and the knowledge qualifier all apply.
- *Buyer wants:* **Tax:** a standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, including under the Completion Accounts cut-off) and full tax warranties, 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure; pre-Completion tax returns and ATO correspondence reviewed. **IP:** full IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, all contractor/employee IP assigned, open-source compliance, Ironquay chain of title), with a separate cap (100%) and 6-year period given the business is an analytics company whose value is its IP and data.
- *Recommendation:* Treat tax and IP as open, not settled; carve both out of the general regime with their own caps and periods. — Reason: the Seller's own Disclosure Letter shows IP title to SOW3 is unresolved and is silent on tax entirely, so "settled" simply means "not negotiated".
